But for the start of this I'm concerned about the translation and the latest one that's caused me to raise this is that plainly in English he used the singular and yet the witness cops back and says the difficulty is he's using the plural. Now, how did that happen, can you tell me? Did you get a plural translation instead of a singular of JSO?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The plural was introduced by Mr. Stamp. He mentioned several units, whereas there was one. Otherwise, it was interpretation, but one unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He used that -- well, anyway, if you can't assist, then that's fine. We'll move on. Mr. Stamp, with this witness in view of what's happened so far, please ask questions that are not leading questions and please let him give us the evidence, otherwise we'll be here forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, apart from regular police units, were there special police units that operated in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Kosovo in 1998 and 1999, there was one special operations unit which was subordinated to the state security department. The head of the RDB in 1998 was Jovica Stanisic up until the 5th of November, 1999; on that day, he was replaced by Mr. Radomir Markovic as the head of the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In its operations in Kosovo, did this unit receive tasks or instructions from the MUP staff for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: I have no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, apart from that unit, were there other special units created to fight the -- what was known as the KLA that were subordinated to the MUP staff of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: There were the regular special anti-terrorist units within the city SUP of Belgrade, the SUP of Novi Sad, and the SUP of Pristina. Those units were sent to intervene in 1998 and 1999, or rather, they took part in the anti-terrorist operations undertaken in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How were the SUP organised in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: Do you mean an individual SUP or as the umbrella organisation or the various SUPs covering the territory of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let's start with your SUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you move on to that, you gave us a date for the changeover from Stanisic to Markovic. Could you give me the date again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During 1998 until the 5th of November, 1998, the head of the RDB was Jovica Stanisic. As of the 5th of November 1998 onwards, the RDB was headed by Radomir Markovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please excuse me for asking you that, but the translation we originally got was November 1999. So thank you for clarifying that. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I return to the special anti-terrorist unit briefly. Was there one unit or more than one unit organised in relation to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: The special anti-terrorist units were not set up specifically for Kosovo. These are peacetime units which fall under the aforementioned secretariats of Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina. However, during the anti-terrorist operations and in times of immediate threat of war, they were engaged in the area of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there other groups engaged in Kosovo in 1999 known as operational sweep group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which organ or body was this group subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where's the base for this claim that these groups were groups sweep -- operational sweep groups?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the witness has given his answer and you'll have a chance to cross-examine. That's not a matter that we can resolve -- but you can assist us to resolve it by the questions you ask in due course. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, I was just asking you to which body or organ was this group subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: In Kosovo in end 1998 - or to be more precise - in December, there were so-called operational sweep or pursuit groups, which comprised people from the special police units. Each of the SUPs gave a number of people, up to ten, and those units were then trained especially to address terrorism. They were better trained and better equipped than the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the head of this group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: There was several groups. There was one group in each of the secretariats; however, the head of all the groups was Mr. Radosavljevic, a.k.a. Guri. Goran Radosavljevic, a.k.a. Guri.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also mentioned that there were also special police units. Were these units known as the PJP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: The PJP were not special police units. The special units of the police -- well, that name could only be borne by the special anti-terrorist units within the state security department and the only other one could have been the JSO, which fell under the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there a police unit known as the PJP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was its role and function?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: The PJP units were formed in early 1992 to cover the area of the secretariat as a whole. They were formed in Belgrade. There was one detachment there, another one in Novi Sad, a third one in Kragujevac as well as Nis and Pristina. They were 450 to 500 men strong each.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. These were manned from the regular police units, but they were better trained and equipped than the regular units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You say they were formed in 1992 -- the units were formed in 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those were separate militia units within the secretariats. They comprised men from several secretariats, however their seat or their command -- commands were in the aforementioned cities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, what were their roles and functions in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999, that is the PJP units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: The PJP units were engaged in Kosovo and Metohija during 1998 and 1999 solely to fight terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To which organ or body were they subordinate, that is those that operated in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC
utterances.text: These were manoeuvreing units commanded by the MUP headquarters or MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could you find a suitable place to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This would be a suitable time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvetic, we have to stop there for today, and your evidence will continue tomorrow; that will be at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon, and we shall then be in a different courtroom, in Courtroom III in this building. So you need to be there, ready to continue your evidence, at 2.15 tomorrow. Meanwhile it's very important that overnight you have no discussion with anyone about your evidence. You can meet with and talk to anyone you wish as long as you do not at any stage discuss the evidence in the case, that's either the evidence you have given or the evidence you may yet give in the case. Could you now please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall see you again tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The court is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of December, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
